summary: Mauro Maggi works in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and under Ronald Eric Emmerick, later holding posts at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East and Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2018).

Mavis L. Fenn works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the Universities of Winnipeg and Calgary, earning her Ph.D. at McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen. She held posts at St. Paul's University College (2005–2006) and the University of Waterloo (attested 2016).

Max Arthur Macauliffe (1841–1913) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He was educated at Springfield College and the University of Galway, where he completed a B.A. between 1857 and 1863.

Max Deeg works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, completing his habilitation at the University of Würzburg (1979–1986). He has held positions at Nagoya University (1992–1997), the University of Vienna (2002–2005), Cardiff University (2006), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Max Hunter Harrison (1893–1986) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Knox College, Andover Newton, Harvard, and Columbia. His career included teaching at Jaffna College (~1918–1920), serving as Principal of United Theological College, Bangalore (1931–1958), and directing the Missionary Research Library (1966–1967).

Max Jakob Niedermann (1874–1954) was a linguist who studied at Zurich and Basel (Ph.D. 1897) under Jacob Wackernagel, later studying with Antoine Meillet, Louis Havet, and Rudolf Thurneysen. He held faculty posts at the University of Basel (1899–1911) and the University of Neuchâtel (1903–1944).

Max Kaltenmark (1910–2002) worked in Sinology and religious studies. He directed the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études Sinologiques (1946) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953), and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris (~1957–1979).

Max Leopold Margolis (1866–1932) specialized in linguistics and religious studies after earning his Ph.D. at Columbia University (1889–1891). He held appointments at Columbia (1891), Hebrew Union College (1892–1897, 1905), the University of California (~1897–1907), and Dropsie College (1909–1932).

Max Lindenau specialized in Indology. He studied at the universities of Munich and Greifswald in 1906, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch by 1913, and served as a Privatdozent at the University of Marburg from 1919 to 1927.

Max Oidtmann is a historian, Sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Carleton College, Indiana University Bloomington, and Harvard University under Mark Elliott. He taught at Georgetown University, including its Qatar campus (2013–2021), before becoming a professor at the University of Munich in ~2021.

Max Scheler (1874–1928) was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Jena. He held academic positions at the University of Jena (~1900–1906), Munich (~1907–1910), Göttingen (~1910–1911), and Cologne (~1919–1928).

Max Walleser (1874–1954) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (Ph.D. ~1900–1902), he taught at Heidelberg University from 1911 to 1936 and founded the Heidelberg Institute for Buddhology in 1928.

Max Weber (1864–1920) worked in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Heidelberg, Strasbourg, Berlin, and Göttingen, he held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1894–1896), Heidelberg University (~1896–1903), the University of Vienna (~1918), and the University of Munich (~1919–1920).

Maximilian Bittner (1869–1918) was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Vienna from approximately 1888 to 1893 under the instruction of Friedrich Müller.

Maximilian Enger (b. 1823) was an Indologist. He completed his Ph.D. studies at the University of Bonn around 1847 to 1851 and subsequently served as a Privatdozent at the same institution from 1852 to 1861.

Maximilian Hoth is an Indology and Buddhist studies researcher who completed an M.A. at the University of Hamburg (2023–2025). He is a doctoral candidate affiliated with the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the University of Munich (attested 2026).
May Oung (1880–1926) was an active figure in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Cambridge from approximately 1904 to 1907. In 1910, he founded the Burma Research Society.

Maya Jasanoff (b. 1974) is a historian who completed studies at Harvard University, the University of Cambridge, and Yale University. She held a post at the University of Virginia (~2003–2009) before becoming a history professor at Harvard University in ~2009.

Maya Keller-Grimm (1899–1990) was an active figure in Buddhist studies. Between approximately 1956 and 1990, she served as the leader of the Altbuddhistische Gemeinde and worked as an editor for the publication Yāna.

Mayum Chonying Wangmo Dorji (1897–1994) worked in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as a member of its General Council from 1964 to 1965.
